structured_output.summary: Both attempt-1 highs are genuinely fixed on changed source. scripts/observe-release.py now selects max(created_at,id) across bounded pages, retains a digest-bound status snapshot and producer hash, with real negative regressions (newer failure/pending, equal-time, across-pages, order independence). The composed delivery guard was actually executed (exit 0, 49 jobs) and is re-executed and bound inside tools/postdelivery.py's governance report; the portable route re-downloaded the published 0.2.4 archive and matched its checksum. Fresh post-publication tag observations on both remotes, run-30/31 documentation, mirror governing text and README-link regressions are implemented and asserted. Residual issues: phase-status delivery.ci_receipt now names an observation file that release_delivery.py's own regex rejects, so the canonical guard is unusable in this tree; an orphan composed-delivery receipt; a governance allowlist superset; and dense, inconsistent style in tools/test_postdelivery.py.

findings.description: verify() requires delivery.ci_receipt to match `docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-\d+\.json`, but docs/phase-status.json:8914 now points ci_receipt at `phase-28-remote-ci-run-31-observation-02.json`. Tag receipts gained separate `tag_observation`/`github_tag_observation` keys (8915-8916) while the CI observation replaced its original key in place, so `python3 tools/release_delivery.py --phase 28 --version 0.2.4` as documented in docs/RELEASE.md:276 now fails in this checkout, and the non-budget advance path at tools/review_phase.py:582 would fail for an ordinary phase-28 review rather than reject for a stated reason. Nothing in phase-status references the original run-31 receipt any more.
findings.required_fix: Model the CI observation like the tags: add a distinct `ci_observation` key, restore `ci_receipt` to docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-31.json, and read the fresh observation from the new key in tools/postdelivery.py:186; or widen the regex to accept observation receipts and assert both namings in tools/test_release_delivery.py. Note the governance-mode-only invocation in docs/RELEASE.md near line 276.

findings.description: GOVERNANCE_PATHS is a superset of the actual governance change set: `tools/test_postdelivery_review.py` does not exist in the repository, and `tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py` is exempted from byte identity yet is never executed by commands_for() (tools/postdelivery.py:212), so a change to it would carry no execution evidence in the current-source report.
findings.required_fix: Drop the nonexistent `tools/test_postdelivery_review.py` entry, and either remove `tools/test_phase_checkpoint.py` from the allowlist or add it to commands_for() so every mutable governance file is covered by an executed suite; assert the allowlist/suite relationship in tools/test_postdelivery.py.

findings.description: This retained guard execution receipt is referenced by no tool, test or document (only the chunk scope list and the review prompt). Its schemaVersion/stdoutSha256 fields are never validated, so it is decorative; the machine-validated equivalent is the canonicalGuard block produced inside docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery.json.
findings.required_fix: Either bind this receipt (path and digest) from tools/postdelivery.py and docs/post-publication-governance.md with a regression in tools/test_postdelivery.py, or remove it and rely solely on the canonicalGuard record.

findings.description: terminal_ci pages /statuses/{sha} until a short page and verifies only its own captured snapshot. The retained snapshot shows pagination instability (id 343 appears at docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-31-observation-02.json:37 and :1488), so a concurrently inserted row could shift pages and be missed; a newer failure added after capture is also undetectable. Run-level `status == 'success'` (line 166) is the only independent corroboration.
findings.required_fix: Record the observation window and either re-observe and compare two snapshots, or page by a stable key and assert the per-context row count is monotonic across the two passes; document the point-in-time limitation in docs/post-publication-governance.md.

findings.description: `prior_failed_ci_observation`/`prior_failed_ci_run` (run 30) are still read by no tool; the guards accept a successful run for the commit without requiring the preserved earlier-failure record or asserting that no later non-success run exists for it. The failure is documented honestly in docs/CI.md:374-385 but only by prose.
findings.required_fix: Have tools/postdelivery.py (or release_delivery.verify) require the retained prior-failure receipt for the delivery commit and reject a later non-success run for the same commit, with a regression in tools/test_release_024.py.

findings.description: The new suite is written in a dense semicolon/one-line style with no spaces around assignment (e.g. :26, :34, :44, :103) that diverges sharply from sibling suites such as tools/test_final_delivery_review.py and tools/test_release_024.py; tools/test_release_023.py:222-224 also gained compound one-line statements. This raises the cost of auditing fail-closed governance assertions.
findings.required_fix: Reformat tools/test_postdelivery.py and the new tools/test_release_023.py branches to the surrounding one-statement-per-line style, keeping the same assertions.

evidence: Prior high #1 fixed in-fingerprint: scripts/observe-release.py:92-109 selects max((created_at,id)) per context, rejects naive timestamps (:100-102) and conflicting equal-key rows (:105-106); :112-129 verify_status_snapshot rebinds producer, statusSelection, observerSha256 and snapshotSha256 and requires the complete success matrix; a `verify-ci` CLI mode exists (:216, :231-236). Regressions in tools/test_release_023.py:208-253 add new-failure, new-pending, equal-time and across-pages modes plus snapshot tampering, and :255-266 assert order independence and naive-timestamp rejection.

The fix is load-bearing on real data: docs/checks/phase-28-remote-ci-run-31-observation-02.json:16-21 shows ws-tracing/1.89.0 id 341 = pending ahead of id 340 = success in API order, while the selected row is id 343 = success (:37-41). The receipt ends with expectedJobCount 49, counts {success: 49}, contextsMatchConfiguredMatrix true (:1516-1520) and binds reviewedSourceSha256 f9cebee5 plus governanceSourceSha256 be67c5c3 (:1521-1523).

Prior high #2 fixed with executed evidence: docs/checks/phase-28-composed-delivery-F.json:4-22 records the guard run in the qualified root with exit 0 and jobs 49, and tools/postdelivery.py:178-182 re-executes that exact command inside verify_composed, so docs/reviews/phase-28-chunk-remote-delivery-attempt-02.checks.json:45-63 carries a machine-validated canonicalGuard (sourceCommit 6f18529, ciCommit 56a88d2, jobs 49). The chunk's eight check rows all exit 0 (13+6+14+52+12+17+38 tests).

Published payload separation is byte-exact and tested: tools/postdelivery.py:54-92 compares mode and blob identity of every tracked/untracked path against the 6f18529 tree, allows only GOVERNANCE_PATHS, and permits exactly two workflow byte substitutions (:70-78); tools/test_postdelivery.py:23-49 proves source, new-file, symlink and non-allowlisted changes are rejected.

Post-publication observations are fresh and ordered: docs/checks/release-tag-v0.2.4-observation-02.json and release-tag-github-v0.2.4-observation-02.json both record tagObject 2f7ad298 peeling to 6f18529 at 18:12:57-58, after publishedAt 17:49:15 (docs/checks/release-registry-0.2.4.json:7); tools/postdelivery.py:102-133 requires the new path to differ from the original, the same tagObject, the current observer digest and checkedAt >= publishedAt, with negative cases at tools/test_postdelivery.py:106-129.

Independent public re-verification actually ran: docs/checks/phase-28-postdelivery-contracts.json:2-7 records scope post_publication_governance_ci with registryArchiveSha256 533294fe..., produced by tools/postdelivery.py:289-298, which downloads static.crates.io with no redirects and a 32 MiB bound and compares bytes/length with the immutable registry receipt; the same file states it does not execute the external qualified checkout.

Findings 3-5 governing text and regressions are implemented, not just claimed: docs/PHASES.md:306-312, docs/typescript-035-parity-plan.md:160-166 and docs/RELEASE.md:225-240 record the mirror destination, fourth receipt, full-history disclosure and tag-before-publish order; docs/CI.md:374-395 documents run 30's deadline failure, the reproduction's explicit non-claim, run 31's selection and the (created_at, id) rule; tools/test_release_024.py:53-69 asserts the README v0.2.4 guide link, all four phrases in three governing documents, both tag commands preceding `cargo +1.99.0 publish`, and the CI.md phrases.

The separate final-delivery budget is tightly bounded: tools/review_phase.py:67-94 requires the single 2026-10-22 grant with the exact question id and answer and pins all twenty original readiness artifacts to FINAL_DELIVERY_ORIGINALS_SHA256; :99-101 isolates the phase-28-final-delivery-attempt-NN namespace; :121 denies the fifth-attempt exception when a budget is used; tools/test_final_delivery_review.py:81-173 drives real orchestration, grant/original tampering, namespace binding and consumed failed attempts.

Governance status is not overclaimed: docs/phase-status.json:7791-7792 and :8306 keep phase 28 in_progress with both chunks pending, :8918-8931 marks the attempt-1 corrections as pending re-review, and docs/post-publication-governance.md:69-81 records that run 31 establishes no scheduler root cause, that Pages deployment and directional live acceptance remain unverified, and that 0.2.4 publication does not complete phases 24/25.
